calls.head: Don’t buy Saros’ record against the Avalanche
calls.body: Saros has been a wall against the Avalanche since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Saros isn’t that wall tonight.

calls.head: Tilted ice, toward the Predators’ net
calls.body: The Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Predators near the bottom. Expect the Avalanche to spend more of the night in the Predators’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Stamkos wins it in overtime
paras: Ross Colton got the scoring started for the Predators early in the first, but Jaden Schwartz tied it up for Colorado midway through the period. Vitali Pinchuk, undrafted and in his seventh NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Reid Schaefer, later in the period to put the Preds back ahead 2-1. Parker Kelly tied it 2-2 for Colorado early in the second. Steven Stamkos won it on the power play a little over two minutes into overtime.

The Avalanche outshot the Predators 32-25, but the Predators’ chances were the more dangerous ones. Justus Annunen made 30 saves for the Predators, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 22 of 25 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Ryan O'Reilly, even with Stamkos’s overtime winner in the game, by our Swing measure. The Predators improved to 7-4-5, fifth in the Central, while the Avalanche dropped to 9-6-2, fourth in the Central.

items.text: Steven Stamkos moved into a tie for seventh on the NHL’s all-time list of overtime goals, with 18.
